final_candidates.decision_summary: Moderate Alphamissense pathogenicity supports transport loss, but low ESM-1v plausibility creates residual folding uncertainty.
Strongest balance among top candidates between LOF potential and limited evolutionary/sequence support, though folding risk remains.
High pathogenicity signal suggests strong transport disruption, but near-zero sequence plausibility lowers confidence in preserved folding.

stop_reason.detail: All four tool-call slots have been used and no additional evidence would likely change the final Top-3 selection.

history.rationale: F160 is a conserved aromatic residue in the predicted substrate translocation pore; alanine removal should abolish cation-pi substrate interactions while leaving helix packing mostly intact.
F160A is sequence-plausible and MSA-tolerated but AlphaMissense is benign, suggesting it may not abolish transport; downranked sharply.
Functional annotation is low-applicability contextual evidence (app=0.2) with no per-position effect; no change.
W216 likely lines the substrate-binding cavity; removing its bulky aromatic side chain is expected to block substrate transport without necessarily disrupting folding.
W216A has a pathogenic LOF-proxy score and the highest MSA tolerance among the aromatic candidates, so it best balances transport ablation with some folding tolerance.
Functional annotation is low-applicability contextual evidence (app=0.2) with no per-position effect; it does not support changing confidence or ranking.
Y220 is a pore-lining tyrosine likely involved in substrate hydrogen bonding/aromatic interactions; alanine substitution should severely impair transport.
Y220A has a strong LOF-proxy score but lower MSA tolerance and zero PLM plausibility, so it is a solid but folding-riskier candidate.
Functional annotation is low-applicability contextual evidence (app=0.2) with no per-position effect; no change.
W260 is a conserved tryptophan at a predicted extracellular gate region; alanine replacement is likely to abolish substrate recognition while preserving overall topology.
W260A has the strongest AlphaMissense LOF signal but extremely poor sequence/evolutionary support, implying likely folding/abundance loss; downranked despite high LOF.
Functional annotation is low-applicability contextual evidence (app=0.2) with no per-position effect; no change.
F354 is an aromatic residue near the extracellular vestibule of the transporter; alanine substitution is expected to disrupt substrate entry or binding.
F354A has a strong LOF-proxy score and MSA tolerance comparable to W216A, making it a top candidate despite low PLM plausibility.
Functional annotation is low-applicability contextual evidence (app=0.2) with no per-position effect; no change.
W490 is a pore-facing tryptophan in the C-terminal transmembrane region; removing it should impair substrate translocation while likely maintaining folding.
W490A has only an ambiguous LOF-proxy score and weak evolutionary support, so it drops in priority.
Functional annotation is low-applicability contextual evidence (app=0.2) with no per-position effect; no change.
D397 is a charged residue in a transmembrane helix that may form electrostatic interactions with cationic substrates; alanine replacement should abolish this interaction.
D397A gives a moderate LOF-proxy score but low sequence/evolutionary support and unclear functional relevance, so it is retained with modest confidence.
Functional annotation is low-applicability contextual evidence (app=0.2) with no per-position effect; no change.
